variants.name: World Cup (golden set)
variants.description: Questions that each guard a trap a model once fell into (ratios of two different measures, ties, a constant metric, a sparse column), moved from the retired golden-set harness and the answer-quality gate. Select the World Cup PostgreSQL datasource with a saved dataset containing the world_cup tables and views.

variants.name: World Cup (golden set, REST API)
variants.description: The same golden-set questions against the World Cup sample served by a local REST API ('npm run worldcup:api'). Select its REST API datasource with a saved dataset containing the api.world_cup endpoints; reference SQL runs in SQLite over the fetched endpoints.

variants.name: World Cup (golden set, Databricks)
variants.description: The same golden-set questions against the World Cup sample in a Databricks Unity Catalog schema, evals.world_cup ('npm run fixture:databricks -- --fixture world-cup' loads it). Select its Databricks datasource with a saved dataset containing the evals.world_cup tables and views; reference SQL is Databricks SQL.

cases.question: Which three teams completed the highest share of their attempted passes across all matches?
cases.intent: A ratio of two different measures, completed over attempted passes, ranked top three.
cases.notes: Healthy ratio over two genuinely different measures. The regression this guards: an answer that divided a sum by itself reported a perfect rate for every row. A correct answer here must divide completed passes by ATTEMPTED passes, so the rates differ per team.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT t.common_name, SUM(s.passes_completed)::numeric / SUM(s.passes_attempted) AS pass_accuracy FROM world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY pass_accuracy DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 3
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT t.common_name, CAST(SUM(s.passes_completed) AS REAL) / SUM(s.passes_attempted) AS pass_accuracy FROM api.world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN api.world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY pass_accuracy DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 3
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT t.common_name, SUM(s.passes_completed) / SUM(s.passes_attempted) AS pass_accuracy FROM `evals`.world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN `evals`.world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY pass_accuracy DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 3

cases.question: Which three teams put the highest share of their shots on target?
cases.intent: The same two-measure ratio on a different column pair, shots on target over shots.
cases.notes: Second two-measure ratio, on a different column pair, so a fix that special-cases passes does not pass this one.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT t.common_name, SUM(s.shots_on_target)::numeric / SUM(s.shots) AS shot_accuracy FROM world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY shot_accuracy DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 3
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT t.common_name, CAST(SUM(s.shots_on_target) AS REAL) / SUM(s.shots) AS shot_accuracy FROM api.world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN api.world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY shot_accuracy DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 3
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT t.common_name, SUM(s.shots_on_target) / SUM(s.shots) AS shot_accuracy FROM `evals`.world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN `evals`.world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY shot_accuracy DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 3

cases.question: Which team scored the most goals in total?
cases.intent: Ranking with an unambiguous winner (France, 14 goals), named rather than reported as an id.
cases.notes: Unambiguous ranking: France lead on 14 with no tie at the top, so a correct answer cannot be a coin toss.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT t.common_name, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM world_cup.goals g JOIN world_cup.teams t ON t.id = g.scoring_team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY goals DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 1
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT t.common_name, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM api.world_cup.goals g JOIN api.world_cup.teams t ON t.id = g.scoring_team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY goals DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 1
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT t.common_name, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM `evals`.world_cup.goals g JOIN `evals`.world_cup.teams t ON t.id = g.scoring_team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY goals DESC, t.common_name LIMIT 1

cases.question: Which teams scored exactly four goals in total?
cases.intent: A tie asked for explicitly: every team on exactly four goals, not one of them.
cases.notes: Ties are real here — Belgium and England both scored 4, and four more teams tie on 2. A 'top 5 scorers' answer would have to break that tie arbitrarily; asking for the tie explicitly makes the expected result deterministic.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT t.common_name, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM world_cup.goals g JOIN world_cup.teams t ON t.id = g.scoring_team_id GROUP BY t.common_name HAVING COUNT(*) = 4 ORDER BY t.common_name
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT t.common_name, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM api.world_cup.goals g JOIN api.world_cup.teams t ON t.id = g.scoring_team_id GROUP BY t.common_name HAVING COUNT(*) = 4 ORDER BY t.common_name
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT t.common_name, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM `evals`.world_cup.goals g JOIN `evals`.world_cup.teams t ON t.id = g.scoring_team_id GROUP BY t.common_name HAVING COUNT(*) = 4 ORDER BY t.common_name

cases.question: What types of disciplinary cards were recorded, and how many of each?
cases.intent: A breakdown where only one value occurs: every card recorded is a yellow.
cases.notes: Every card in the data is a yellow, so any 'share that were yellow' metric is 1 on every row — the constant-metric trap. The honest answer states that only yellows were recorded rather than reporting a meaningless 100%.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT card_type, COUNT(*) AS cards FROM world_cup.disciplinary_events GROUP BY card_type ORDER BY cards DESC, card_type
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT card_type, COUNT(*) AS cards FROM api.world_cup.disciplinary_events GROUP BY card_type ORDER BY cards DESC, card_type
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT card_type, COUNT(*) AS cards FROM `evals`.world_cup.disciplinary_events GROUP BY card_type ORDER BY cards DESC, card_type

cases.question: How many goals have a recorded assisting player?
cases.intent: A sparse column: count the goals that have an assist instead of grouping by a mostly blank key.
cases.notes: Assists are recorded on only 2 of 47 goals, so grouping by assisting player buries 45 goals under a blank key. A correct answer counts the goals that HAVE an assist rather than silently presenting the blank group as a finding.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT COUNT(*) AS goals_with_assist FROM world_cup.goals WHERE assist_player_id IS NOT NULL
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT COUNT(*) AS goals_with_assist FROM api.world_cup.goals WHERE assist_player_id IS NOT NULL
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT COUNT(*) AS goals_with_assist FROM `evals`.world_cup.goals WHERE assist_player_id IS NOT NULL

cases.question: How many goals were scored of each goal type?
cases.intent: Control: a categorical breakdown with no ratio and no nulls.
cases.notes: Categorical breakdown with no ratio and no nulls — a control. If this fails, the problem is schema linking, not the guards.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT goal_type, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM world_cup.goals GROUP BY goal_type ORDER BY goals DESC, goal_type
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT goal_type, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM api.world_cup.goals GROUP BY goal_type ORDER BY goals DESC, goal_type
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT goal_type, COUNT(*) AS goals FROM `evals`.world_cup.goals GROUP BY goal_type ORDER BY goals DESC, goal_type

cases.question: What was the total match attendance for each tournament year?
cases.intent: Control: a plain aggregate over a join.
cases.notes: Plain aggregate over a join — the healthy baseline. Guards must stay silent on this one.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT tr.tournament_year, SUM(m.attendance) AS total_attendance FROM world_cup.matches m JOIN world_cup.tournaments tr ON tr.id = m.tournament_id GROUP BY tr.tournament_year ORDER BY tr.tournament_year
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT tr.tournament_year, SUM(m.attendance) AS total_attendance FROM api.world_cup.matches m JOIN api.world_cup.tournaments tr ON tr.id = m.tournament_id GROUP BY tr.tournament_year ORDER BY tr.tournament_year
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT tr.tournament_year, SUM(m.attendance) AS total_attendance FROM `evals`.world_cup.matches m JOIN `evals`.world_cup.tournaments tr ON tr.id = m.tournament_id GROUP BY tr.tournament_year ORDER BY tr.tournament_year

cases.question: How many matches were played at each stage of the tournaments?
cases.intent: A full breakdown whose smallest groups tie (final and third place, 2 matches each).
cases.notes: Ties at the bottom (final and third_place both 2) — a 'least common stage' phrasing would be ambiguous, so the question asks for the full breakdown.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT stage, COUNT(*) AS matches FROM world_cup.matches GROUP BY stage ORDER BY matches DESC, stage
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT stage, COUNT(*) AS matches FROM api.world_cup.matches GROUP BY stage ORDER BY matches DESC, stage
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT stage, COUNT(*) AS matches FROM `evals`.world_cup.matches GROUP BY stage ORDER BY matches DESC, stage

cases.question: What share of their attempted passes did each team complete?
cases.intent: A share for every team built from two different measures, completed over attempted passes; the rates must differ by team.
cases.notes: Moved from the answer-quality gate (scripts/check-answers.ts, check pass-completion-ratio). It guards the production bug: the same measure aliased twice and divided by itself, narrated as a flat rate. Ground truth varies by team (Croatia 0.871, Brazil 0.870, England 0.869), so a correct answer cannot be uniform. The gate accepted the share computed in SQL or in the prose; the result-set check compares rows, so it needs the share in the SQL result, as an unrounded fraction. Reference SQL written for the move (BA-182); it returned 12 rows on the World Cup fixture on 2026-10-13.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT t.common_name, SUM(s.passes_completed)::numeric / SUM(s.passes_attempted) AS pass_completion FROM world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY t.common_name
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT t.common_name, CAST(SUM(s.passes_completed) AS REAL) / SUM(s.passes_attempted) AS pass_completion FROM api.world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN api.world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY t.common_name
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT t.common_name, SUM(s.passes_completed) / SUM(s.passes_attempted) AS pass_completion FROM `evals`.world_cup.match_team_statistics s JOIN `evals`.world_cup.teams t ON t.id = s.team_id GROUP BY t.common_name ORDER BY t.common_name

cases.question: What share of the disciplinary cards shown were yellow?
cases.intent: A share that is 100% everywhere: the answer must say every card was a yellow rather than compare teams.
cases.notes: Moved from the answer-quality gate (scripts/check-answers.ts, check constant-metric-not-compared). It guards invented variation: breaking down a metric that is 100% on every row as if teams differed. Every card in the fixture is a yellow (8 of 8). The gate checked that the answer mentions yellow and says all, only or 100%. The reference returns the two counts the share is built from (8 yellow cards of 8), because the share itself may be written as 1 or as 100. Reference SQL written for the move (BA-182); it returned 1 row on the World Cup fixture on 2026-10-13.

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE card_type = 'yellow') AS yellow_cards, COUNT(*) AS total_cards FROM world_cup.disciplinary_events
expectedSql.sqlite: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN card_type = 'yellow' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS yellow_cards, COUNT(*) AS total_cards FROM api.world_cup.disciplinary_events
expectedSql.databricks: SELECT COUNT_IF(card_type = 'yellow') AS yellow_cards, COUNT(*) AS total_cards FROM `evals`.world_cup.disciplinary_events
